message.reasoning:
I am playing Monopoly as an AI player.

I have $51 cash and am on Pennsylvania Avenue after paying $150 rent. My holdings include three mortgaged properties and three streets with one house each. Other players have substantial cash and full monopolies.

Player 4 has a full green monopoly with one house on each property. I cannot mortgage, build, or unmortgage anything. I am considering whether to trade or end my turn.

I am calculating exact rent values to assess the risk. One house on Illinois pays $100, while one house on Pennsylvania pays $150. I need to determine whether trading or selling houses is the better move.

Player 2 now holds a full pink monopoly and can build houses immediately next turn. Player 3 has substantial cash but no monopoly.

I cannot build or unmortgage anything. Selling all three houses would return only $225, but I need the rent income from them. I will keep my houses and end my turn.

I am evaluating trade options. Neither player can complete a light-blue or orange monopoly without my mortgaged properties. The red streets remain my only income source.

Player 4 cannot afford to build more houses on their green monopoly. I am now considering selling one house for $75 to increase my cash buffer, since $51 is too low to survive another large rent.

Selling one house is legal since the remaining two would still differ by only one. Trading Vermont or New York for cash is unlikely to work. Neither player can complete a light-blue or orange monopoly without both properties, and Player 2 has no interest in either.

I am now reconsidering trading. I will propose a trade to Player 2 for cash in exchange for Vermont or New York, since I cannot afford to sell my red houses.

Player 2 is unlikely to overpay for a mortgaged property, since they need cash to build their pink monopoly. Player 3 has $867 but still needs unowned properties to complete any set.

Player 3 probably will not pay much for a mortgaged property that does not complete a set. Player 4 has no spare cash to trade for Vermont, since they mortgaged everything to build their green monopoly.

Player 2 has no interest in my mortgaged properties, so trading with them is unlikely to help. I will end my turn now rather than sell houses or offer trades, since $51 is tight but I have already paid rent and can survive another roll.

Player 3 might pay $200–$400 for mortgaged New York. That would give me $351 and allow building houses. I am checking whether I can actually build.

I realized that enabling Player 3's orange monopoly would create three monopolies against my reds. I will not trade New York for cash.

Player 2 can build two houses on each pink street for $600, leaving them with $51. Player 3 could build five houses on their orange set for $500, leaving them with $51. I will keep my houses and only sell them if the engine forces a debt resolution.
